name: DataTable
usage:
Lists of records with server-side sorting and pagination, file and asset lists, large logs, tables that
users arrange themselves

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table, such as "Projects".

props.name: columns
props.description:
The columns, in their default order. While the rows are sorted locally (by a column with `compare`), they are
sorted again whenever this array changes: inline columns sort them on every render, which is fine for most
tables. For many rows, define the columns outside the component or with `useMemo`, so that they change only when
what they read changes.

props.name: rows
props.description: The rows (the current page when paginated).

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Stable key of a row, such as its ID.

props.name: sort
props.description:
Current sorting (controlled); `null` when not sorted. Use it with `onSortChange`, for example to sort on the
server.

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: Initial sorting (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called when a sortable header is clicked: none, then ascending, then descending, then none again.

props.name: selectable
props.description: Adds a selection column with a checkbox in each row and a "select all" checkbox in the header.

props.name: selectedKeys
props.description:
Keys of the selected rows (controlled); use it with `onSelectionChange`. Keys of rows that are not in `rows`
(other pages) are kept.

props.name: defaultSelectedKeys
props.description: Keys of the rows selected at first (uncontrolled).

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Called with the new keys when the selection changes.

props.name: isRowSelectable
props.description:
Whether a row can be selected; rows that cannot have a disabled checkbox and are skipped by "select all". All
rows are checked again whenever this function changes: an inline function checks them on every render, which is
fine for most tables. For many rows, pass a stable function (`useCallback`) that changes when what it reads
changes.

props.name: rowLabel
props.description:
Name of a row for screen readers, such as its title: the checkbox is read as "Select Alex Morgan". Without
it, the content of the first column is used.

props.name: columnSettings
props.description:
Shows the column settings button on the right of the toolbar: users can show and hide columns, change their
order, pin them, and restore the defaults.

props.name: storageKey
props.description:
Saves the column widths, order, visibility and pinning on this device (in `localStorage` under this key) and
restores them on the next visit. Use a key that is unique in your application, such as `'files.table'`.
Saved columns that no longer exist are ignored; new columns appear as defined.

props.name: height
props.description:
Height of the table area in pixels (without the toolbar and the footer): the rows scroll inside it and the
header stays at the top.

props.name: fill
props.description:
Fills the height of the parent (a flex column or an element with a height): the rows scroll inside and the
header stays at the top.

props.name: virtual
props.description:
Renders only the visible rows. On by default with `height` or `fill` and more than 100 rows; it needs one of
them to know the visible area.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Loading: the current rows stay, and a loading indicator appears on top of them after 200 ms (fast loads do
not flash). Without rows, the indicator takes the place of the empty state.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error state shown instead of the rows: a text readable by users (never the raw exception), or `true` for the
default title only.

props.name: onRetry
props.description: Retry in the error state: when provided, a "Retry" button is shown.

props.name: empty
props.description: Shown when there are no rows, instead of the default empty state.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Toolbar on the left above the table: search, filters, actions for the whole table.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Content below the table, such as Pagination. Leave it out while there are no rows: a pager for an empty list
only shows "0" and page 1.

props.name: bulkActions
props.description:
Actions for the selected rows (usually Buttons). While rows are selected, the toolbar row is replaced in place
by a SelectionBar with the number of selected rows, "Clear selection" and these actions; the content below does
not move. Needs `selectable`.

props.name: totalCount
props.description:
Number of all rows (all pages), when the table shows one page. Passed to the SelectionBar: it says "All N
selected" once everything is selected, and offers "Select all N" before that with `onSelectAll`. When some
rows cannot be selected (`isRowSelectable`), pass the number of rows that can.

props.name: onSelectAll
props.description: Selects all rows of all pages (offered by the SelectionBar when `totalCount` is larger than the selection).

props.name: onRowClick
props.description:
Called when a row is clicked (not when clicking a link, a button, a checkbox or another control in it, or
when selecting text). Rows are not focusable: also put a link or a button that does the same thing in the
main column, so that keyboard and screen reader users can open the row.

fields.name: key
fields.description:
Stable identifier of the column: used for sorting, for the saved width, order, visibility and pinning, and as
the default cell value (`row[key]`).

fields.name: label
fields.description:
Plain-text name of the column, used in the column settings and by screen readers (resize handle, row
checkboxes). Required when `title` is not a string; defaults to `title` when it is one.

fields.name: render
fields.description: Renders the cell. Without it, the cell shows `row[key]` as text.

fields.name: align
fields.description: Horizontal alignment of the header and the cells; use `end` for numbers so that they line up.

fields.name: width
fields.description: Default width in pixels. Columns without a width share the remaining space (at least 120 px each).

fields.name: minWidth
fields.description: Smallest width in pixels when resizing.

fields.name: maxWidth
fields.description: Largest width in pixels when resizing.

fields.name: pin
fields.description:
Pins the column to the start or the end: it stays in place while the other columns scroll horizontally. A
pinned column without `width` is 160 px wide. Users can change it in the column settings.

fields.name: sortable
fields.description:
The header can be clicked to sort by this column. Rows are sorted locally only when `compare` is given;
otherwise sort them yourself (for example on the server) using `onSortChange`.

fields.name: compare
fields.description:
Compares two rows for local sorting (ascending order; descending is derived). Implies `sortable`. It sorts the
rows passed in `rows` only: when the table shows one page of a longer list, sort the whole list yourself
(controlled `sort` and `onSortChange`) before cutting out the page, or sort on the server.

fields.name: hideable
fields.description:
Whether users can hide the column in the column settings. Set `false` for the main column (such as the
name), which is always shown.

fields.name: defaultHidden
fields.description: Hidden at first; users can show it in the column settings.

fields.name: truncate
fields.description:
Truncates the cell content to one line with an ellipsis; the full text appears in a tooltip, but only when
the text is actually cut off.

fields.name: resizable
fields.description: Whether the width can be adjusted by dragging the edge of the header or with the keyboard.

types.name: DataTableSort
types.summary:
The current sorting of a DataTable: which column and in which direction. `null` (in `sort`, `defaultSort` and
`onSortChange`) means not sorted.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
Columns with `compare` can be sorted by clicking their header (or with `Enter` on it); numbers use
`align: 'end'`. Drag the edge of a header, or focus it with `Tab` and press `←` / `→`, to change a column width.
Place the table in a Panel with `flush`.

examples.name: Selection
examples.title: Selection and bulk actions
examples.description:
`selectable` adds a checkbox to each row; the header checkbox selects every row shown and is mixed when only
some are. `Shift`-click selects a range. Finished projects cannot be selected here (`isRowSelectable`). With
`bulkActions`, the toolbar row turns into a bar with the count, "Clear selection" and the actions while rows are
selected; archiving runs right away and can be undone from the message.

examples.name: Pinned
examples.title: Pinned columns
examples.description:
`pin` keeps a column at the start or the end while the others scroll horizontally; a faint line appears where
content passes under it. A typical use is an actions column pinned to the end. Columns without `width` share
the remaining space.

examples.name: States
examples.title: Empty, loading and error
examples.description:
Without rows the default empty state is shown (or `empty`); while the first page loads, the loading indicator
takes its place after 200 ms; `error` with `onRetry` shows the error state with a "Retry" button. The header
stays visible in every state.

examples.name: ServerSide
examples.title: Server-side sorting and pagination
examples.description:
With `sort` and `onSortChange` the server sorts: give the columns `sortable` instead of `compare`. Pagination
goes in `footer` and search in `toolbar`. While a page loads, the current rows stay and the loading indicator
appears only after 200 ms; the main column holds a link, so keyboard users can open a row as well.

examples.name: SavedColumns
examples.title: Column settings saved on this device
examples.description:
`columnSettings` adds a button on the right of the toolbar to show and hide columns, change their order, pin
them and restore the defaults. With `storageKey`, these choices and the column widths are kept on this device.
`hideable: false` keeps the main column visible; `defaultHidden` hides a column until users show it.

examples.name: LargeData
examples.title: Large data
examples.description:
With `height` (or `fill`) and more than 100 rows, only the visible rows are rendered: ten thousand rows scroll
smoothly, the header stays at the top and the pinned column stays in place.
